The query’s very low neutral fraction, 0.02 versus 0.9995 in the neighbor, also reflects a much more ionized molecule, which is not automatically favorable on its own. Even with those counterpoints, the added tertiary amine and lower PSA make Neighbor 1 overall a useful substrate-like analogue, though it is not perfectly one-sided.

The only clearly opposing feature is that the neighbor contains 1H-indole while the query does not, which by itself favors the non-substrate side. Even so, the basic amine, stronger pKa, higher partial charge, and increased sp3 character together keep Neighbor 2 firmly on the substrate side.

Neighbor 3 is also strongly supportive of the substrate assignment. The query again has one tertiary aliphatic amine while the neighbor has none, reinforcing the basic-center motif that is repeatedly associated with CYP2D6 substrates. The query’s strongest basic pKa is 9.0913 compared with 9.1947 in the neighbor, so the delta is only -0.1034, and the two molecules are very close on this descriptor; the query still sits in a strongly basic range. The neighbor also has an aryl bromide that the query lacks, and in this local comparison that substituent is not enough to outweigh the query’s more compact profile. Taken together, the query’s protonatable amine plus its lower heteroatom burden and lower size fit better with the substrate side here, so Neighbor 3 points clearly toward the final substrate label.

Neighbor 4 is the first of the non-substrate neighbors, but most of its direct feature differences still resemble the query and therefore actually favor substrate behavior. The neighbor carries morpholine and an aryl chloride, while the query does not, and the query’s fraction of sp3 carbons is the same as the neighbor’s at 0.4615, so shape alone does not separate them. Even though this neighbor is labeled non-substrate overall, the comparison itself shows several query features that are more consistent with CYP2D6 substrate chemistry, so Neighbor 4 still lends substantial support to the substrate prediction rather than undermining it.

Neighbor 5 is the clearest non-substrate counterexample, and it highlights why the final decision is not based on a single descriptor. The query’s fraction of sp3 carbons is higher, 0.4615 versus 0.2632, which also trends toward the more substrate-like end of this local comparison. The neighbor also has an aryl chloride, which the query lacks. Because the neighbor has no basic site at all and the ionization/charge features cut against the substrate-like pattern, Neighbor 5 is legitimately negative evidence, even though some individual query features remain favorable.

Neighbor 6 again shows a mixture, but the overall comparison leans to the substrate side on several core features while still containing some opposition. Even so, the shared tertiary amine, the higher basic pKa, and the lower flexibility keep this neighbor from overturning the broader substrate pattern entirely; it is a negative neighbor overall, but one with several query features that still look substrate-like.

Putting the six comparisons together, the strongest recurring signal is the query’s protonatable tertiary aliphatic amine, along with generally favorable basicity and a reasonably substrate-like balance of size, shape, and polarity in several of the positive-neighbor comparisons. The negative neighbors do introduce real counterevidence, especially the low logD in Neighbor 6 and the unusual ionization pattern in Neighbor 5, but even those comparisons still preserve important substrate-like elements such as the basic amine and higher pKa. Overall, the positive-neighbor evidence is more consistent and more directly aligned with the CYP2D6 substrate motif, so the final prediction is option (B): is a substrate to the enzyme CYP2D6.
